title: Finite subfamilies of global generators on a compact open
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], V and K opens with K contained in V and K compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let H be an O_X-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] of finite type on K [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and let sigma be a specified global generating family for H restricted to V (an epimorphism from the free sheaf on sigma.I). There is a finite subset S of sigma.I such that the free map on S, followed by the given generating epimorphism, becomes epimorphic upon restriction from V to K. Neither V affine nor H quasi-coherent is assumed.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BB (17.9.7), proof: local finite generators, local lifts and finite subcover, specialized to the directed union of finite-generated image subsheaves of a specified global generating family; Lemma 01B8 (17.9.4). Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01BB and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01B8.

proof.text: For x in K, choose finitely many local generators of H on a neighbourhood inside K. The epimorphism from the specified global free sheaf locally lifts them. Each germ of a section of the free sheaf is a finite linear combination of its basis germs: the free sheaf is the filtered colimit of its finite sub-coproducts, and stalks commute with filtered colimits. The finitely many lifts therefore have a common finite support S_x. Their germ identities hold on a common smaller neighbourhood; on that neighbourhood the finite-support map is epi because its image contains every local generator. This is the local lifting argument of Stacks 01B8 and 01BB. No finite presentation, affine localization, or quasi-coherence is used.

The neighbourhoods just constructed cover K. Choose finitely many using compactness, and let S be the union of their finite supports. For each selected neighbourhood, the free map for S_x factors through the free map for S. Thus the latter is epi on every selected neighbourhood. Local surjectivity, equivalently surjectivity on stalks, proves that its restriction to K is epi. The slice restriction functor and its free-module comparison identify this with the overMap expression in Lean. When K is empty choose the empty finset; if the original index type is empty, its epimorphism already identifies H on V with zero.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 01BB, proof, finite-cover argument applied to finite subsets of a global generating family; the local shrinking is Lemma 01B8.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finset_generatingSections_on_compact
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (V K : X.Opens) (hK : IsCompact (K : Set X)) (hKV : K ≤ V)
    (H : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
    [(H.over K).IsFiniteType] (σ : (H.over V).GeneratingSections) :
    ∃ S : Finset σ.I,
      Epi ((SheafOfModules.overMap (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE hKV)).map
        (SheafOfModules.freeMap (R := (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V)
          ((↑) : S → σ.I) ≫ σ.π))
